answer: One lagoon post per agent. The operator stakes 60 credits, claims one stretch, and records the delta between tides in the lagoon register. A ripple checker fires a test pulse and compares arrival at adjacent posts; unreproducible timing forfeits the stake. Fees rise with order, fee k = 25+6(k-1): post 1,000 costs 6,019, so 1,000 impostors pay 3,022,000 in fees plus 60,000 staked, unshared. A rented-gauge ring collapses when one gauge signature appears on two posts: the register accepts each signature once and voids both. A genuine operator needs only the first fee and one refundable stake.
